verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：
verses.en: The Lord spoke to Moses:

verses.zh: 「你还要晓谕以色列人说：凡以色列人，或是在以色列中寄居的外人，把自己的儿女献给摩洛的，总要治死他；本地人要用石头把他打死。
verses.en: “You are to say to the Israelites, ‘Any man from the Israelites (or any of the resident foreigners[NOTE:1] who live in Israel) who gives any of his children[NOTE:2] to Molech[NOTE:3] must be put to death; the people of the land must pelt him with stones.[NOTE:4]
notes: The noun “foreigner” (גֵּר; ger) is based on the same verbal root as “lives” (גּוּר; gur), which means “to sojourn, to dwell as an alien.” On the Hebrew ger (גֵּר) “resident foreigner” see notes at Exod 12:19 and Deut 29:11.
Heb “his seed” (so KJV, ASV); likewise in vv. 3-4.
Regarding Molech and Molech worship see the note on Lev 18:21.

This is not the most frequently-used Hebrew verb for stoning (see instead סָקַל, saqal), but a word that refers to the action of throwing, slinging, or pelting someone with stones (רָגָם, ragam; see HALOT 1187 s.v. רגם qal.a, and B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 136).
verses.commentary:
20:2 This chapter's introductory phrase is different from previous chapters. The VERB "say,"
"speak" is not an IMPERATIVE.

verses.zh: 我也要向那人变脸，把他从民中剪除；因为他把儿女献给摩洛，玷污我的圣所，亵渎我的圣名。
verses.en: I myself will set my face[NOTE:1] against that man and cut him off from the midst of his people,[NOTE:2] because he has given some of his children to Molech and thereby defiled my sanctuary and profaned my holy name.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “And I, I shall give my faces.”
On the “cut off” penalty see the notes on Lev 7:20 and 17:4.
Heb “for the sake of defiling my sanctuary and to profane my holy name.”
verses.commentary:
20:3 "I will set My face" See note at Lev. 17:10. This is a repeated phrase (cf. Lev. 20:3,5,6).

▣ "I will cut him off from among his people" See note at Lev. 17:10.

▣ "so as to. . ." Notice how idolatry affects Israel.

- defiles YHWH's sanctuary (BDB 379, KB 375, Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT;
cf. Lev. 15:31; Num. 19:13,20)

- profanes YHWH's name (BDB 320, KB 319, Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT; cf. Lev. 18:21)

verses.zh: 那人把儿女献给摩洛，本地人若佯为不见，不把他治死，
verses.en: If, however, the people of the land shut their eyes[NOTE:1] to that man[NOTE:2] when he gives some of his children to Molech so that they do not put him to death,
notes: Heb “And if shutting [infinitive absolute] they shut [finite verb].” For the infinitive absolute used to highlight contrast rather than emphasis see GKC 343 §113.p.
Heb “from that man” (so ASV); NASB “disregard that man.”
verses.commentary:
20:4

NASB
"should ever disregard"

NKJV
"should in any way hide their eyes"

NRSV
"should even close their eyes"

TEV, Peshitta
"ignores"

NJB
"choose to close their eyes"

JPSOA, NET
"shut their eyes"

REB
"connive at it"

LXX
"should by an oversight overlook with their eyes"

This VERB (BDB 761, KB 834) is linked to the INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE
of the same root, which intensifies the thought. The "hiding" can be of the

- eyes ‒ 1 Sam. 12:3; Ps. 10:1; Pro. 28:27; Isa. 1:15; Ezek. 22:26

- ears ‒ Lam. 3:56

- fact ‒ 2 Kgs. 4:27

- council ‒Job 42:3

Here, it denotes someone who knows a fellow Israeli has given his child (lit. "seed") to Molech and does
not tell the proper authorities will be put to death. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY.

verses.zh: 我就要向这人和他的家变脸，把他和一切随他与摩洛行邪淫的人都从民中剪除。
verses.en: I myself will set my face against that man and his clan. I will cut off from the midst of the people both him and all who follow after him in spiritual prostitution,[NOTE:1] committing prostitution by worshiping Molech.[NOTE:2]
notes: The adjective “spiritual” has been supplied in the translation to clarify that this is not a reference to literal prostitution, but figuratively compares idolatry to prostitution.
Heb “to commit harlotry after Molech.” The translation employs “worshiping” here for clarity (cf. NAB, NCV, TEV, CEV, NLT). On the “cut off” penalty see the note on Lev 7:20.
verses.commentary:
20:5 "set My face against that man" See note at Lev. 17:10.

Notice that several people are to be put to death (probably by the stoning of the whole community, Lev. 20:2).

- the one who sees the idolatry and does not tell

- the family (wife, children, grandchildren) of the one who does not tell

- the ones involved in the idolatry

- although not specifically mentioned, the family of the one giving his children to Molech because they would have known.

I have two comments about this.

- This is an example of Hebrew corporality. One's actions affect the whole (Exod. 20:5; Joshua 7).

- This must also be seen in light of Ezekiel 18, where only the sinner is affected.

- This is typical biblical paradox. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: PARADOX IN SCRIPTURE.

▣ "playing the harlot after Molech" This refers to "spiritual adultery" by the fact that YHWH was Israel's
true husband (see SPECIAL TOPIC: FATHER)
and, therefore, when Israel went after other gods it was a symbol of her going "awhoring after other gods" (cf. Exod. 34:15-16;
Lev. 17:7; Deut. 31:16; Jdgs. 2:17; 8:27,33; Jer. 3:1; Ezek. 20:30; Hos. 2:7).

verses.zh: 「人偏向交鬼的和行巫术的，随他们行邪淫，我要向那人变脸，把他从民中剪除。
verses.en: “‘The person who turns to the spirits of the dead and familiar spirits[NOTE:1] to commit prostitution by going after them, I will set my face[NOTE:2] against that person and cut him off from the midst of his people.
notes: For structure and coherence in Lev 20:6-27 see the note on v. 27 below.
See the note on the phrase “familiar spirits” in Lev 19:31 above.
verses.commentary:
20:6 "medium and spiritists" See Lev. 19:26,31; 20:27; Deut. 18:10-12. See full notes online in Deuteronomy 19.

20:6 This is the key theological concept of Leviticus (cf. Lev. 11:14; 19:2; 20:24). Israel was uniquely YHWH's
people by covenant, not just creation.

verses.zh: 所以你们要自洁成圣，因为我是耶和华―你们的　神。
verses.en: “‘You must sanctify yourselves and be holy, because I am the Lord your God.
verses.commentary:
20:7 "consecrate" This is the Hebrew term kadosh (BDB 872, KB 1073, Hithpael
PERFECT with waw). It is the VERB form of "holy" (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY). This is
demanded several times in Leviticus (cf. Lev. 11:44; 19:2; 20:7,26).

This concept is parallel to (1) "sanctifies" (BDB 872, KB 1073, Piel PARTICIPLE)
in Lev. 20:8 (2) "separated" (BDB 95, KB 110) in Lev. 20:24,25, literally, "to divide.

Israel made a distinction between what was clean and unclean (Lev. 20:25; Leviticus 11;
Deuteronomy 14). Israel was to be different from her surrounding pagan nations. She was to reflect YHWH's holiness!

verses.zh: 你们要谨守遵行我的律例；我是叫你们成圣的耶和华。
verses.en: You must be sure to obey my statutes.[NOTE:1] I am the Lord who sanctifies you.
notes: Heb “I will give my faces.”
verses.commentary:
20:8 "keep" Notice the number of times in Leviticus this is stated (cf. Lev. 8:35; 18:4,5,26,30; 19:3,19, 30, 37;
20:8,22; 22:9,31; 25:18; 26:2,3; and many more times in Deuteronomy. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP and
SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT.

▣ "statutes" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

▣ "the Lord" This is covenant language. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "sanctifies" Notice the parallel concepts of

- be holy, Lev. 20:7

- sanctify, Lev. 20:8

- separate, Lev. 20:24-25

YHWH sanctified them but Israel must "practice" (BDB 793, KB 889, Qal PERFECT
with waw) them!

All the doctrines of the Bible involve God's sovereignty and mankind's free will. See
SPECIAL TOPIC:
ELECTION/PREDESTINATION AND THE NEED FOR A THEOLOGICAL BALANCE and
SPECIAL TOPIC:
PREDESTINATION (CALVINISM) AND HUMAN FREE WILL (ARMINIANISM) and
SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT.

verses.zh: 凡咒骂父母的，总要治死他；他咒骂了父母，他的罪（原文是血；本章同）要归到他身上。
verses.en: “‘If anyone[NOTE:1] curses his father or mother,[NOTE:2] he must be put to death. He has cursed his father or mother; his blood guilt is on himself.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “And you shall keep my statutes and you shall do them.” This appears to be a kind of verbal hendiadys, where the first verb is a modifier of the action of the second verb (see GKC 386 §120.d, although שָׁמַר [shamar, “to keep”] is not cited there; cf. Lev 22:31, etc.).
Compare the regulations in Lev 18:6-23.
Heb “If a man a man who.”
verses.commentary:
20:9 "curses his father or his mother" This is the opposite of "honor" (cf. Exod. 20:12 and would encompass
Exod. 21:15). See note at Lev. 19:3. This shows the significance of family stability as it relates to long term societal stability.
Note the parallel in Deut. 21:18-21.

verses.zh: 「与邻舍之妻行淫的，奸夫淫妇都必治死。
verses.en: If a man[NOTE:1] commits adultery with his neighbor’s wife,[NOTE:2] both the adulterer and the adulteress must be put to death.
notes: Heb “makes light of his father and his mother.” Almost all English versions render this as some variation of “curses his father or mother.”

The rendering “blood guilt” refers to the fact that the shedding of blood brings guilt on those who shed it illegitimately (even the blood of animals shed illegitimately, Lev 17:4; cf. the background of Gen 4:10-11). If the community performs a legitimate execution, however, the blood guilt rests on the person who has been legitimately executed (see the remarks and literature cited in J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 328).tn Heb “his blood [plural] is in him.” Cf. NAB “he has forfeited his life”; TEV “is responsible for his own death.”
verses.commentary:
20:10-21 This deals with sexual abuses mentioned in chapter 18. See full note there.

- Lev. 20:10 ‒ Lev. 18:20

- Lev. 20:11 ‒ Lev. 18:7,8

- Lev. 20:12 ‒ Lev. 18:15

- Lev. 20:13 ‒ Lev. 18:22

- Lev. 20:14 ‒ Deut. 27:23

- Lev. 20:15 ‒ Lev. 18:23

- Lev. 20:16 ‒ Lev. 18:23

- Lev. 20:17 ‒ Lev. 18:9

- Lev. 20:18 ‒ Lev. 18:19

- Lev. 20:19 ‒ Lev. 18:12,13

- Lev. 20:20 ‒ Lev. 18:14

- Lev. 20:21 ‒ Lev. 18:16

Leviticus 18 defines the boundaries and chapter 19 the consequences for disobedience.

20:10 The word "adultery" (BDB 610, KB 158) is used four times.

- Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE

- Same as 1.

- adulterer

- adulteress

All require the death penalty.

This verse seems to have a redundant phrase which may be the result of an early copyist's error. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: TEXTUAL CRITICISM.

verses.zh: 与继母行淫的，就是羞辱了他父亲，总要把他们二人治死，罪要归到他们身上。
verses.en: If a man goes to bed with[NOTE:1] his father’s wife, he has exposed his father’s nakedness.[NOTE:2] Both of them must be put to death; their blood guilt is on themselves.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “And a man who.” The syntax here and at the beginning of the following verses elliptically mirrors that of v. 9, which justifies the rendering as a conditional clause.

The reading of the LXX minuscule mss has been followed here (see the BHS footnote a-a). The MT has a dittography, repeating “a man who commits adultery with the wife of” (see the explanation in J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 328). The duplication found in the MT is reflected in some English versions, e.g., KJV, ASV, NASB, NIV.
Heb “lies down with.” The verb שָׁכַב (shakav) “to lie down” acts as a euphemism, implying going to bed for sexual relations.
verses.commentary: 20:11 See note at Lev. 18:7,8 and at Contextual Insights, C.

verses.zh: 与儿妇同房的，总要把他们二人治死；他们行了逆伦的事，罪要归到他们身上。
verses.en: If a man goes to bed[NOTE:1] with his daughter-in-law, both of them must be put to death. They have committed perversion;[NOTE:2] their blood guilt is on themselves.
notes: See the note on Lev 18:7 above.
See the note on v. 9 above.
verses.commentary:
20:12 See note at Lev. 18:15 and at Contextual Insights, C.

▣

NASB, TEV, JPSOA
"incest"

NKJV, NRSV
"perversion"

NJB, REB
"violated nature"

LXX
"behaved impiously"

Peshitta
"committed a sin"

This term (BDB 117) basically means "confusion" in the sense of the NJB, REB (cf. Lev. 18:23; 20:12).

verses.zh: 人若与男人苟合，像与女人一样，他们二人行了可憎的事，总要把他们治死，罪要归到他们身上。
verses.en: If a man goes to bed with[NOTE:1] a male as one goes to bed with a woman,[NOTE:2] the two of them have committed an abomination. They must be put to death; their blood guilt is on themselves.
notes: Heb “lies down with.” See note at v. 11.
The Hebrew term תֶּבֶל (tevel, “perversion”) derives from the verb “to mix; to confuse” (cf. KJV, ASV “they have wrought confusion”).
verses.commentary:
20:13 See note at Lev. 18:22 and at Contextual Insights, C.

▣ "a detestable act" This (BDB 1072) is used earlier in Lev. 7:18; 11:10; 18:22,26,27,29. See notes there.
See SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION (OT)
and SPECIAL TOPIC: HOMOSEXUALITY.

For a brief discussion of the Bible's condemnation of homosexuality, see Hard Sayings of the Bible,
pp. 543-545.

verses.zh: 人若娶妻，并娶其母，便是大恶，要把这三人用火焚烧，使你们中间免去大恶。
verses.en: If a man has marital relations with both a woman and her mother,[NOTE:1] it is lewdness.[NOTE:2] Both he and they must be burned to death,[NOTE:3] so there is no lewdness in your midst.
notes: Heb “lies down with.” See note at v. 11.
Heb “[as the] lyings of a woman.” The specific reference here is to homosexual intercourse between males.

Heb “takes a woman and her mother.” The verb לָקַח (laqakh) is sometimes used idiomatically with אִשָּׁה (ʾishah) to mean “take a wife,” or “marry,” and may mean that here (cf. NIV, NASB). But the same expression in v. 21 probably does not imply marriage itself, but only the sexual act of marriage. This chapter uses different expressions for sexual relations, though the subtleties for exegesis are not clear. Since this Hebrew expression can imply marriage, the translation uses “marital relations” as the metaphor in vv. 14, 17, and 21.
verses.commentary:
20:14 "they shall be burned with fire" Fire was one way to cleanse. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE.

▣ There are several verses that require the burning of law breakers (cf. Gen. 38:24; Lev. 20:14; 21:9). Also,
Saul's and his sons' bodies were burned in 1 Sam. 31:12-13. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: CREMATION.

verses.zh: 人若与兽淫合，总要治死他，也要杀那兽。
verses.en: If a man has sexual relations[NOTE:1] with any animal, he must be put to death, and you must kill the animal.
notes: Regarding “lewdness,” see the note on Lev 18:17 above.
verses.commentary: 20:15 See note at Lev. 18:23 and at Contextual Insights, C.

verses.zh: 女人若与兽亲近，与它淫合，你要杀那女人和那兽，总要把他们治死，罪要归到他们身上。
verses.en: If a woman approaches any animal to copulate with it, you must kill the woman, and the animal must be put to death; their blood guilt is on themselves.
verses.commentary: 20:16 See note at Lev. 18:23 and at Contextual Insights, C.

verses.zh: 「人若娶他的姊妹，无论是异母同父的，是异父同母的，彼此见了下体，这是可耻的事；他们必在本民的眼前被剪除。他露了姊妹的下体，必担当自己的罪孽。
verses.en: “‘If a man has marital relations with[NOTE:1] his sister, whether the daughter of his father or of his mother, so that he sees her nakedness and she sees his nakedness, it is a disgrace. They must be cut off in the sight of the children of their people.[NOTE:2] He has exposed his sister’s nakedness; he will bear his punishment for iniquity.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “in fire they shall burn him and them.” The active plural verb sometimes requires a passive translation (GKC 460 §144.f, g), esp. when no active plural subject has been expressed in the context. The present translation specifies “burned to death” because the traditional rendering “burnt with fire” (KJV, ASV; NASB “burned with fire”) could be understood to mean “branded” or otherwise burned, but not fatally.
See the note on Lev 18:20 above.

The Hebrew verb לָקַח (laqakh) “to take” sometimes means to take a woman in marriage (cf. Gen 34:16; Lev 20:14; and see HALOT 534 s.v. לקח) as understood by, e.g., NIV, NCV, TEV, CEV. It is possible that expression here simply means to have sexual relations, or that it does so in combination with the following two clauses. See note at v. 14.

verses.zh: 妇人有月经，若与她同房，露了她的下体，就是露了妇人的血源，妇人也露了自己的血源，二人必从民中剪除。
verses.en: If a man goes to bed[NOTE:1] with a menstruating woman and uncovers her nakedness, he has laid bare her fountain of blood, and she has exposed the fountain of her blood, so both of them[NOTE:2] must be cut off from the midst of their people.
notes: Regarding the “cut off” penalty, see the note on Lev 7:20.
See the note on Lev 17:16 above.

verses.zh: 不可露姨母或是姑母的下体，这是露了骨肉之亲的下体；二人必担当自己的罪孽。
verses.en: You must not expose the nakedness of your mother’s sister or your father’s sister, for such a person has exposed his own close relative.[NOTE:1] They must bear their punishment for iniquity.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “lies down with.” See note at v. 11.
Heb “and the two of them.”

verses.zh: 人若与伯叔之妻同房，就羞辱了他的伯叔；二人要担当自己的罪，必无子女而死。
verses.en: If a man goes to bed[NOTE:1] with his aunt, he has exposed his uncle’s nakedness; they must bear responsibility for their sin, they will die childless.
notes: Heb “his flesh.”
verses.commentary:
20:20,21 "They will be childless" For a Jewish family to be childless even affected their afterlife (NIDOTTE,
vol. 3, pp. 534-535). In this chapter this is the result of "cut off" (i.e., the family line ceases; see note at Lev. 7:20).

verses.zh: 人若娶弟兄之妻，这本是污秽的事，羞辱了他的弟兄；二人必无子女。
verses.en: If a man has marital relations with[NOTE:1] his brother’s wife, it is indecency. He has exposed his brother’s nakedness;[NOTE:2] they will be childless.
notes: See the note on Lev 17:16 above.
Heb “lies down with.” See note at v. 11.

verses.zh: 「所以，你们要谨守遵行我一切的律例典章，免得我领你们去住的那地把你们吐出。
verses.en: “‘You must be sure to obey all my statutes and regulations,[NOTE:1] so that[NOTE:2] the land to which I am about to bring you to take up residence does not vomit you out.
notes: Heb “takes.” See notes at vv. 14 and 17. sn It must be assumed that the brother is still alive in this situation, since Deut 25:5 requires a man to marry his brother’s widow and have a child in his brother’s name. It is less clear whether the brother in this case has divorced his wife.
See the note on Lev 18:7 above.
verses.commentary:
20:22 "to keep" See SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP
and SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT.

▣ "My statutes and all My ordinances" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S
REVELATION.

▣ "the land. . .will not spew you out" As Israel's sin made the Tabernacle ceremonially unclean, so Israel's sin
made the land unclean. The land is personified as spewing out (cf. Lev. 18:28) the Hebrews as it had the Canaanites (cf. Lev. 20:23
and Gen. 15:16).

verses.zh: 我在你们面前所逐出的国民，你们不可随从他们的风俗；因为他们行了这一切的事，所以我厌恶他们。
verses.en: You must not walk in the statutes of the nations[NOTE:1] which I am about to drive out before you, because they have done all these things and I am filled with disgust against them.
notes: Heb “And you shall keep all my statutes and all my regulations and you shall do them.” This appears to be a kind of verbal hendiadys, where the first verb is a modifier of the action of the second verb (see GKC 386 §120.d, although שָׁמַר [shamar, “to keep”] is not cited there; cf. Lev 22:31, etc.).
verses.commentary:
20:23 "I have abhorred them" This VERB (BDB 880, KB 1089, Qal
IMPERFECT) means "to feel disgust." In the Pentateuch it is used in several senses.

- Gen. 27:46 ‒ Rebekah was distraught over her Canaanite daughter-in-law

- Exod. 1:12; Num. 22:3 ‒ the Egyptians feared the Israelites because of their numbers

- Num. 21:5 ‒ the Israelites were sick and tired of the manna they had to eat every day

- here, the VERB is theologically parallel to

- "abhor" (BDB 1055, KB 1646, cf. Lev. 20:25)

- "loath" (BDB 1072, KB 1702); cf. Gen. 43:32; 46:34; Exod. 8:26; Ps. 95:10; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION (OT)

verses.zh: 但我对你们说过，你们要承受他们的地，就是我要赐给你们为业、流奶与蜜之地。我是耶和华―你们的　神，使你们与万民有分别的。
verses.en: So I have said to you: You yourselves will possess their land and I myself will give it to you for a possession, a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the Lord your God who has set you apart from the other peoples.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and.” The Hebrew conjunction ו (vav, “and”) can be considered to have resultative force here.
verses.commentary:
20:24 "a land flowing with milk and honey" This phrase describes the agricultural abundance of Canaan.
It is mentioned several times.

- YHWH's initial call to Moses, Exod. 3:8,17

- consecration of the firstborn after the 10th plague on Egypt, Exod. 13:5

- YHWH's message about the conquest by the power of YHWH's special angel, Exod. 33:3

- the spies sent into Canaan, Num. 13:27; 14:8

- remember all the victories and blessings were a gift from YHWH, Deut. 8:7-10; 31:20

- an allusion to Gen. 15:12-22 ‒ Exod. 11:9

- consecration and giving of first fruits after the conquest, Deut. 26:9

- write the law on the stones from Jordan, Deut. 31:20

- just after crossing Jordan, Josh. 5:6

▣ "separated" The terms "holy," "set apart," and "separated" have a similar root idea—that which is given
to God for His special use. The people of God are holy because they have been set apart as a kingdom of priests (cf.
Lev. 20:26; Exod. 19:5-6; 33:16). Israel was meant to bring the whole world to God. God has revealed Himself through Israel.
One of the real problems with Israel's lack of faith is that she affects the whole world. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL
REDEMPTIVE PLAN.

verses.zh: 所以，你们要把洁净和不洁净的禽兽分别出来；不可因我给你们分为不洁净的禽兽，或是滋生在地上的活物，使自己成为可憎恶的。
verses.en: Therefore you must distinguish[NOTE:1] between the clean animal and the unclean, and between the unclean bird and the clean, and you must not make yourselves detestable by means of an animal or bird or anything that creeps on the ground—creatures[NOTE:2] I have distinguished for you as unclean.[NOTE:3]
notes: One medieval Hebrew ms, Smr, and all the major ancient versions have the plural “nations.” Some English versions retain the singular (e.g., KJV, ASV, NASB, NRSV); others have the plural “nations” (e.g., NAB, NIV) and still others translate as “people” (e.g., TEV, NLT).
Here and with the same phrase in v. 26, the LXX adds “all,” resulting in the reading “all the peoples.”

Heb “And you shall distinguish.” The verb is the same as “set apart” at the end of the previous verse. The fact that God had “set them apart” from the other peoples around them called for them to “distinguish between” the clean and the unclean, etc.
verses.commentary:
20:25 "You are therefore to make a distinction" This is the essence of the concept of "holiness" in Leviticus.
YHWH is "separate"; they, too, should be different from their pagan neighbors in every area of life. Leviticus 20:25, like
Leviticus 11; Deuteronomy 14, deals with food.

The VERB translated "make distinction" (BDB 95, KB 110, Hiphil
PERFECT with waw is exactly the same for as the last VERB of Lev. 20:24,
"I have separated." The basic meaning of the VERB is "to divide."

- separate Israel from the other nations, Lev. 20:24

- separate Israel's food, clean from unclean, Lev. 20:25

- in Exod. 26:33 it is used of the veil that separates the "Holy of Holies" from the "Holy Place" of the inner shrine of the Tabernacle

- in Num. 16:9 it is used of the priests being separated to serve YHWH (i.e., they took the place of the firstborn, cf. Exodus 13)

notes: The word “creatures” has been supplied in the translation to make it clear that the following relative clause modifies the animal, bird, or creeping thing mentioned earlier, and not the ground itself.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- As Leviticus 18 and 19 deal with specific definitions of improper acts of covenant partners, chapter 20 deals with the
consequences of sins.

- Leviticus 20:2-5 deals with Molech, who is first mentioned in Lev. 18:21. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: MOLECH and
SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP
OF THE ANE.

- This chapter uses an intensified grammatical structure (i.e., INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and
IMPERFECT VERB of the same root).

- Lev. 20:2 ‒ "shall surely be put to death" (BDB 559, KB 562)

- Lev. 20:4 ‒ "should ever disregard" (lit. "should ever hide," BDB 761, KB 834)

- Lev. 20:9 ‒ same as #1

- Lev. 20:11 ‒ same as #1

- Lev. 20:12 ‒ same as #1

- Lev. 20:13 ‒ same as #1

- Lev. 20:15 ‒ same as #1

- Lev. 20:16 ‒ same as #1

- Lev. 20:27 ‒ same as #1

There are terrible consequences to disobedience in time and eternity. YHWH wants a "holy"
people to reflect His character to a pagan world (cf. Lev. 11:44; 19:2; 20:7,24,26)

- A good list of death penalty (i.e., by stoning) cases would be

- premeditated (non-legal) murder ‒ Exod. 21:12; Lev. 24:17; Num. 35:16-21

- kidnaping ‒ Exod. 21:16; Deut. 24:7

- idolatry ‒ Exod. 22:19; Lev. 20:1-5; Deut. 13:2-19; 17:2-7 (cursed in Deut. 27:15)

- blasphemy ‒ Lev. 24:14-16,23

- profane the sabbath ‒ Exod. 31:14-15

- sorcery ‒ Exod. 22:17; Lev. 20:27

- prostitution involving a priest's family ‒ Lev. 21:9

- dishonoring parents ‒ Exod. 21:15,17; Lev. 20:8; Deut. 21:18-21 (cursed in Deut. 27:16)

- adultery ‒ Lev. 20:10; Deut. 22:22

- incest ‒ Lev. 20:11,12,14,17 (see Leviticus 18)

- homosexuality ‒ Lev. 20:13

- bestiality ‒ Lev. 20:15-16 (cursed in Deut. 27:21)

Stoning to death by the community was a way to demonstrate Israel as a holy people, a community of
purity which must rid itself of wickedness and law breakers (i.e., Lev. 20:2,27; 24:14-23; Num. 15:35; Deut. 21:21).
